node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Function machine view
node.description: Interpret a function as a process that takes an input and produces a corresponding output.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Evaluate function at an expression
node.description: Evaluate function notation when the input is an algebraic expression rather than a single number.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Domain from denominator restrictions
node.description: Identify input values excluded from a domain because they make a denominator equal zero.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Domain from even root restrictions
node.description: Identify input values allowed by requiring even-root radicands to be nonnegative in real-valued functions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Domain from logarithm argument
node.description: Identify input values allowed by requiring logarithm arguments to be positive.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Interval notation for domains
node.description: Write function domains using interval notation, including open and closed endpoints.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Range from turning points
node.description: Determine a function's range from maximum or minimum turning points visible or known from a graph or rule.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Range from asymptote
node.description: Use horizontal or vertical asymptotic behaviour to describe possible output values of a function.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Outer inner order in composition
node.description: Identify which function is applied first and which is applied second in a composite function.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Composition from tables
node.description: Evaluate composite functions using values from one or more function tables.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Composition from graphs
node.description: Evaluate composite functions by reading outputs from graphs in the correct order.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Inverse from ordered pairs
node.description: Find the inverse relation by swapping coordinates in ordered pairs.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Inverse graph reflection
node.description: Recognise an inverse relation or inverse function graph as a reflection across the line y equals x.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Algebraic inverse steps
node.description: Find a formula for an inverse function by swapping variables and solving for the new output variable.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Piecewise boundary values
node.description: Evaluate piecewise functions at boundary values by using the interval condition that includes the input.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Piecewise graph segments
node.description: Graph a piecewise function by drawing the appropriate segment for each rule and interval.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vertical translation of functions
node.description: Describe how adding a constant outside a function shifts its graph upward or downward.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Horizontal translation of functions
node.description: Describe how replacing x by x minus h or x plus h shifts a graph horizontally.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Function reflections in axes
node.description: Describe reflections in the x-axis and y-axis using negative multipliers outside or inside a function.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Function stretches and compressions
node.description: Describe vertical and horizontal stretches or compressions of function graphs from transformation notation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Denominator cannot be zero
node.description: A real-valued function expression with a denominator is undefined for inputs that make the denominator zero.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Even root radicand must be nonnegative
node.description: For real-valued functions, the expression under an even root must be greater than or equal to zero.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Composition applies inner function first
node.description: In a composite function, the inner function is evaluated before the outer function.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Inverse graph reflects over y equals x
node.description: The graph of an inverse relation is the reflection of the original relation across the line y equals x.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Horizontal transformations reverse sign appearance
node.description: Horizontal translations written inside the function often appear with the opposite sign from the movement direction.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Denominator restriction ignored
node.description: Learner includes an input value that makes a denominator equal zero in the function domain.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Composition order reversed
node.description: Learner evaluates a composite function in the reverse order from the notation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Piecewise wrong interval selected
node.description: Learner evaluates a piecewise function using a rule whose interval condition does not include the input.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Horizontal shift sign reversed
node.description: Learner interprets horizontal shift notation as moving in the same direction as the sign shown inside the function.

edge.rationale: The function machine model directly practises interpreting inputs and outputs.
Denominator restrictions are a core type of domain restriction.
Correct outer-inner order is central to function composition.
Reflecting across y equals x directly represents reversing ordered pairs.
Boundary-value selection is a core part of evaluating piecewise functions.
Horizontal translations directly practise interpreting transformation notation.
Senior function notation builds on earlier linear-function input-output relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats function notation as a multiplication expression or equation label only.

edge.rationale: Evaluating at an algebraic expression extends numerical function evaluation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner substitutes only numbers and cannot preserve algebraic structure.

edge.rationale: Denominator restrictions require understanding domain as allowable input values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner includes undefined input values in the domain.

edge.rationale: Even-root restrictions are another algebraic domain restriction after denominator exclusions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner allows inputs that make the radicand negative for real-valued functions.

edge.rationale: Logarithm-domain restrictions depend on the meaning and definition of logarithms.
edge.failure_signal: Learner allows zero or negative logarithm arguments in real-valued contexts.

edge.rationale: Writing a domain in interval notation depends on understanding the allowed input set.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes endpoint symbols without connecting them to included or excluded values.

edge.rationale: Using turning points to find range builds on reading range from a graph.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives x-values of turning points instead of output bounds.

edge.rationale: Asymptotic range restrictions are advanced graph-range features.
edge.failure_signal: Learner includes an asymptote value as an attainable output without justification.

edge.rationale: Identifying outer-inner order requires understanding composition notation and meaning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner evaluates the functions in the wrong order.

edge.rationale: Table-based composition depends on applying the inner function first and using that output as the next input.
edge.failure_signal: Learner looks up both functions using the original input only.

edge.rationale: Graph-based composition depends on reading function outputs in the correct order.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads the correct graph values but uses them in the wrong order.

edge.rationale: Swapping ordered pairs follows from the meaning of inverse relations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner swaps symbols but not paired input-output values.

edge.rationale: Graph reflection across y equals x is the geometric form of swapping ordered pairs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reflects across the wrong axis or does not swap coordinates.

edge.rationale: Algebraic inverse steps require understanding inverse notation and inverse-function meaning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes reciprocal notation or fails to solve for the output variable.

edge.rationale: Choosing boundary values depends on reading piecewise interval conditions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses the wrong rule at an endpoint.

edge.rationale: Graphing piecewise segments requires selecting correct rules and endpoint inclusion for each interval.
edge.failure_signal: Learner draws full parent graphs instead of restricted pieces.

edge.rationale: Vertical translation is a core case after introducing function transformations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes x-values instead of output values for a vertical shift.

edge.rationale: Horizontal translation is often introduced after the simpler outside-function vertical shift case.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reverses the sign or direction of the horizontal shift.

edge.rationale: Axis reflections are core transformation cases after transformation notation is introduced.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses reflection in the x-axis with reflection in the y-axis.

edge.rationale: Stretches and compressions extend basic transformation notation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats every multiplier as a vertical scale factor or confuses horizontal effects.
